articles.body:
First playthrough. Resolved Peace event, so elephant was in center of Bombay. Resolved Leader, also Bombay, exhausting regiments etc. to make sure that failed. Elephant did not march. Now we have flipped Resolve Crisis, and want to make sure we should just treat this as another Attack against Company? The two options seem to be (p. 32) elephant's tail or elephant's head. Page 7 says that when the elephant is in the center, "the acting region is getting ready to rebel against its sovereign," but no other information on what's up when it's in the center (though we have only read rules once). We're assuming it's an attack against the company, but want to make sure we get it right before next game!

Thanks for any clarification!
Happy holidays.

articles.body:
Adding to Samuel's answer, the order of rules is as follows: in the same page 32, under the title Rebellion, it says
[q="Rules of Play"]If the attacker is a dominated region, resolve a Rebellion.[/q]
In your case, the region is dominated (as it is defined in page 6, and assuming you controlled Bombay). Now, page 33 starts with
[q="Rules of Play"]Both Invasions and Rebellions against Company-controlled regions are resolved the same way.[/q]
So, it would be an attack against the Company, no other forces involved. Finally, page 33 clarifies that the strength of this Rebellion would be the modifier on the ganjifa card plus all unrest cubes in the region.
